messages.subject: Distance matrix from genetic map
parts:
Hi all, 

This is an ignorant question but what is your favorite way to calculate a distance matrix from a genetic map? 

My first thought would be to use dist() but I noticed that this function requires a numeric variable and not a factor (genotype). I can recode the values as 1 and 2 (standard output of cross.object$geno) but I am not sure that is correct mathematically.

Another option would be using an already written package, like 'ape' that does those type of calculations. I'd have to delve into the details to see how much reformatting that would require.

How do you do it?

Max

messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] Distance matrix from genetic map
parts:
It depends on what you're trying to do.

The function comparegeno() calculates the proportion of mismatches across markers for all pairs of individuals; you could use this as a distance matrix.

karl

messages.author: 6ea789bedfb0caf8
messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] Distance matrix from genetic map
parts:
Thanks Karl. That is exactly what I was looking for. Here's a simple code example:

###### Distance matrix from an R/qtl cross.object

# Calculate similarity between genotypes
similarity_matrix<-comparegeno(cross.object)

# Add in the RIL line names as row and col names
rownames(similarity_matrix)<-cross.object$pheno[,1]
colnames(similarity_matrix)<-cross.object$pheno[,1]

# Transform similarity matrix into difference matrix
inverted<-similarity_matrix - 1
distance_matrix<-inverted * -1

# Replace 'NA' with 0 (Identical RILs have 0 distance between them)
distance_matrix[is.na(distance_matrix)]<-0

# Can now use to examine dendrogram of RILs
hc<-hclust(as.dist(distance_matrix))
plot(hc, cex=0.45)

###### END 

I'm trying to compare 2 genetic maps of the same RIL self population constructed using different genotyping technologies. They appear almost identical, but any discrepancy between them will be interesting to examine further.

Two ways I can think of doing this is comparing the number and location of breakpoints (XO) within each RIL per build and looking at how similar/different the RILs are from each other as a whole between map assemblies.

Any other suggestions/methods would be greatly appreciated. Thanks again,

Max

parts:
Karl gave me an idea of a quick way to compare 2 genetic maps. 

While I am not sure if this answer is statistically sound (did this on my own) from an analytical perspective it was very useful for identifying discrepancies between the 2. 

Essentially, combine the two maps based upon positional information, impute the genotypes missing in the one map by utilizing the positional information and genotypes called from the other. 

Examine the similarity between individuals using a dendrogram.

I've attached an example. It helped us quickly identify 6 of 219 individuals that warrant further inspection.
